name: MeasuredMoveObjectiveTarget
quote: A rough profit target for the follow-through leg ... is the so-called measured move objective (MMO), which assumes that the CD leg ... will approximately equal the length of the AB leg
description: Profit target for the trend-resumption leg (CD) equals the length of the prior impulse leg (AB), projected from the pullback's extreme (C).
book_order_type: limit at target (mechanized as close-and-next-open once reached, per convention)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to locate points A, B, and C

notes: Grimes explicitly treats this as a rough guideline, not exact; also usable as an entry-area target for the second leg of a complex pullback (G03-17).

name: PivotTargetForPullbackTrade
quote: the pivot high or low (in an uptrend or a downtrend, respectively) of the setup leg is an ideal target and should be considered the first, most conservative profit target for any pullback trade
description: First, conservative profit target for a pullback trade: the pivot extreme of the setup leg preceding the pullback (the prior swing high in an uptrend).
book_order_type: limit at prior pivot (mechanized as close-and-next-open once reached)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection

name: ParallelChannelTakeProfitZone
quote: if you are long in an uptrend and prices rise to the upper parallel trend line, it probably makes sense to be slightly defensive and to take some profits
description: Price reaches the upper parallel trend line (a trend line anchored to the standard trend line's opposite-side pivots) -- take partial profits.
book_order_type: limit at the channel line (mechanized as close-and-next-open once reached)

complexity.reason: needs the parallel-channel projection built on G03-36's pivots

name: FailurePullbackSequenceMeasuredMoveTarget
quote: the move out of the failure pullback often exhausts itself somewhere close to the measured move objective (MMO), thus defining the initial extreme of the new trading range.
description: Target/expectation for the second (renewed) countertrend leg of a failure-pullback sequence: it tends to exhaust near a measured-move projection -- the length of the first countertrend leg added onto the end of the small pullback that followed it.
book_order_type: n/a (profit target, limit at target level)

complexity.reason: needs leg-length measurement from detected swing points

name: MeasuredMoveObjectiveTarget
quote: the measured move objective (MMO), which is calculated by taking the length of the setup leg (AB in Figure 6.8), adding that number to the pivot point marked C, and expecting the CD leg to be approximately the same length as the AB leg.
description: Primitive profit target: project the length of a prior (setup) swing leg forward from a later pivot point, expecting the next leg to be of similar length. Reused as a target by several templates in this file.
book_order_type: n/a (profit target, limit at target level)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to identify leg AB and pivot C

notes: Grimes treats this as a zone, not an exact level: 'consider it a zone... take partial or complete profits even though the trade had not quite reached the target.'

name: FailureTestFirstTargetAtInitialRisk
quote: one plan would be to take profit on the first part when the profit equals the initial risk on the trade.
description: Take (partial) profit once open profit reaches the initial per-share/point risk (entry price to stop price) of the trade.
book_order_type: n/a (limit/market profit exit)

complexity.reason: needs the initial stop distance carried as position state

name: PullbackConservativeTargetPriorSwing
quote: The most conservative profit target is at the previous pivot high of the setup leg for long traders, or at the low of the setup leg for shorts.
description: Take profit at the pivot high (long) / low (short) that started the pullback -- the previous swing extreme.
book_order_type: n/a (limit profit target)

complexity.reason: window highest/lowest

name: PullbackRiskMultipleTarget
quote: it also makes sense to incorporate information from the conservative and MMO profit targets... taking partial profits at one or two times (1x or 2x) the initial risk on the trade.
description: Take (partial) profit at a multiple of the initial risk (entry-to-stop distance) on the trade.
book_order_type: n/a (limit/market profit exit)

complexity.reason: needs the initial stop distance carried as position state

name: ScratchExitOnTrendIntegrityLoss
quote: A pullback may emerge at a spot where the trade was justified, but developing price action may suggest that the trend is losing integrity. If this happens... it is often advisable to scratch the trade, exiting for a small win or loss.
description: If within a few bars of entry a strong bar forms against the trade direction (proxy for 'the trend is losing integrity'), scratch the trade at market rather than holding to the original stop.
pseudocode: ctx.BarsSinceEntry() <= scratchWindow AND (opposite-direction bar body) > bodyMultiple * average(high[1..lookback] - low[1..lookback])
book_order_type: n/a (market scratch exit)

complexity.reason: 'losing integrity' is a qualitative read; mechanized here as an early strong opposite-direction bar

name: ComplexPullbackLegEqualityTarget
quote: both countertrend legs of the pullback tend to be similar lengths, so it is often possible to predict the general area where the second leg will stop using a measured move objective (AB = CD).
description: In a complex pullback, project the second countertrend leg (CD) to be approximately the same length as the first (AB) -- the same MMO mechanics as G06-02, specialized to the two legs of this pattern.
pseudocode: target = pivotCPrice - (legAB_HighPrice - legAB_LowPrice) (mirrored sign for shorts)
book_order_type: n/a (limit profit target / expected reversal zone)

complexity.reason: needs the same swing-pivot detection as G06-27

name: AntiMmoFirstTarget
quote: It is very common to see the first thrust after the initial pullback exhaust itself at the MMO, and then to see the market turn back down and eventually violate the previous trend extreme.
description: Apply the measured-move-objective target (G06-02) to the Anti's first thrust out of the pullback: the length of the countertrend spike projected forward from the pullback's end.
pseudocode: target = pullbackEndPrice - (spikeHighPrice - spikeLowPrice) (mirrored sign for shorts)
book_order_type: n/a (limit profit target / management inflection zone)

complexity.reason: same swing/leg-length requirement as G06-02

name: BaseStopWiderRiskBased
quote: once the market consolidated below that support level... the probabilities began to favor a breakdown and another trend leg down, so there was no sense in riding the trade to the initial stop level.
description: A wider, earlier stop for base entries: exit if price consolidates below (above) the base's own support (resistance) for consolidateBars bars, rather than waiting for the initial (looser) stop.
book_order_type: n/a (management exit, ahead of the hard stop)

complexity.reason: a persistent counter of consecutive closes beyond a level

name: BreakoutBaseMmoTarget
quote: Some traders will set ratio-based targets for breakout trades. Common examples use, for instance, measured move objectives based on the width of the preceding range or the base.
description: Apply the measured-move-objective mechanics (G06-02) to a breakout-base entry: the width of the base (or the larger preceding range) projected forward from the breakout point.
book_order_type: n/a (limit profit target)

complexity.reason: the base width is already available from G06-42's window extremes, no separate pivot detection needed

notes: Grimes notes prebreakout conditions often feature abnormally contracted volatility, so ratio-based targets from the base width alone can be unnecessarily conservative; he generally prefers no fixed target once the trend is confirmed (see G06-56's notes).

name: FailedBreakoutTarget
quote: I tend to be aggressive in taking those profits on failed breakout trades, perhaps even exiting more than half of my position at the first target.
description: Take a larger-than-usual partial profit (more than half the position) once open profit reaches the initial risk on the trade -- the same mechanics as G06-10, with a larger exitFraction noted.
book_order_type: n/a (limit/market profit exit)

complexity.reason: needs the initial stop distance carried as position state

notes: The exact exit fraction ("more than half") is a position-sizing detail, not itself a bar-level condition; only the trigger price is mechanized here.

name: HigherTimeframeMeasuredMoveTargetFilter
quote: One common area of a more predictable spurt occurs when a pattern has broken into a move to a target-for instance, on the drive out of a consolidation pattern or following a strong break of support or resistance... recognizing that a scenario like this is in play can lend support to otherwise uninteresting lower time frame patterns.
description: Adds confidence to a lower-timeframe with-trend consolidation entry when the higher-time-frame-approximated series is mid-drive toward a measured-move target (projected from its own prior swing leg) rather than already having reached it.
book_order_type: n/a (context test)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and a measured-move projection on the higher-time-frame-approximated series

name: ProfitTargetAtOneRiskMultiplePartial
quote: I usually exit between 25 and 33 percent of the position on a limit order at a profit equal to my initial risk in the trade
description: A fraction of the position is taken off at a limit price equal to one initial-risk multiple of profit above the entry.
book_order_type: limit order at entry + 1x risk, working GTC; mechanized as a stop-level test on the bar's extreme

complexity.reason: requires a stopDistance parameter standing in for the actual initial risk, which the engine cannot read back from the entry-side stop rule

notes: The generator's Exit rules likely cannot express a partial-percentage exit natively; exitFraction is recorded for the authoring pass to decide whether to model as a full exit at this level (a simplification) or leave partial sizing out of scope.
stopDistance should mirror whatever the paired Entry/Exit stop rule (e.g. G08-01 or G08-03) uses, or the risk multiple will be inconsistent with the actual initial stop.

name: ProfitTargetAtTwoRiskMultiplesPartial
quote: I also make it a point to be down to between one-third to half my initial size at two times my initial risk, and then manage the remainder according to a different set of rules
description: A second tranche is taken off (leaving roughly one-third to one-half of the original size) at a limit price equal to two initial-risk multiples of profit above the entry.
book_order_type: limit order at entry + 2x risk, working GTC; mechanized as a stop-level test on the bar's extreme

complexity.reason: same stopDistance-parameter caveat as G08-05

notes: Same parameterized rule as G08-05 with riskMultiple=2; kept as a separate candidate because Grimes treats the two tranches as distinct decision points with different downstream management.

name: ProfitTargetCappedAtNearestSwingPivot
quote: If you normally take profits at risk multiples and find yourself entering an order to buy or sell beyond one of these visible points, it probably makes sense to tighten the orders up a little bit and bring them inside the swings
description: When a risk-multiple profit target would fall beyond the nearest visible swing pivot, use the (tighter) swing-pivot-inside offset instead of the risk-multiple level.
pseudocode: targetLevel = min(ctx.EntryPrice() + riskMultiple * stopDistance, swingHigh(pivotIndex, swingStrength) - offsetTicks * ctx.MinMove()) ; high[0] >= targetLevel
book_order_type: limit order at the tighter of the two levels

complexity.reason: composes a risk-multiple target with swing-pivot detection and takes the minimum of the two

notes: A refinement rule layering G08-05/06's risk-multiple target with G08-24's pivot-offset target; the authoring pass may prefer to keep these as two independent Exit rules ORed together rather than one composite, since the pane system already ORs exits.

name: PartialProfitFractionAtFirstTarget
quote: As a matter of discipline, I take profits on between 25 and 50 percent of the position at this first profit target.
description: When open profit reaches the initial risk (the 1R first target -- entry to stop distance, in the direction of the trade), exit a fixed fraction of the position rather than the whole position or none of it. Grimes gives a range (20 to 50 percent depending on aggressiveness) rather than a single number.
book_order_type: limit order at the 1R price (a scale-out), not a stop

complexity.reason: a difference test against a fixed 1R level computed once at entry, plus a partial-size exit

notes: Grimes states a range of 25-50% as his normal discipline, with 20% in rare aggressive cases and 50% when concerned about a trade; defaulted partialFraction to 0.375 (midpoint of the stated normal range) since no single number is given.
This assumes the engine's pane system supports partial exits; if not, the authoring pass should note the limitation.

name: FirstTargetCappedAtNearestSwingLevel
quote: I set my first target at one times my risk in almost all cases, the only exceptions being when that target would be beyond a very visible chart point.
description: The standard first target is 1R, but if the 1R price would lie beyond the nearest visible chart level (a recent swing high/low), use that swing level as the target instead of the full 1R distance.
pseudocode:
// long
naturalTarget = ctx.EntryPrice() + 1.0 * initialRiskDistance
nearestSwingLevel = highest(high, swingLookback)  // most recent swing high above entry, computed at entry time
targetPrice = min(naturalTarget, nearestSwingLevel)
high[0] >= targetPrice
book_order_type: limit order at targetPrice

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to find the nearest visible chart level ahead of the 1R price, not just a fixed-window highest/lowest

notes: approximated 'a very visible chart point' as the nearest swing pivot; Grimes does not define this precisely.

name: ExitPullbackIfFlatAfterNBars
quote: If this assumption is incorrect, the market may simply go flat after the trade is entered, without a significant move up or down. This is strong evidence that the market has temporarily found equilibrium and that whatever edge there might have been in the trade is now gone.
description: If a pullback trade has produced no meaningful directional movement (bar ranges stay compressed, no progress toward target or stop) within N bars of entry, scratch the trade for a small win or loss rather than continuing to hold.
book_order_type: n/a (discretionary scratch, mechanized as a time+range exit)

complexity.reason: needs a bars-since-entry counter and an ATR-scaled measure of how far price has moved since entry

notes: Grimes gives no exact bar count for 'too long to sit in a simple pullback'; defaulted maxFlatBars to 6 as a sensible guess for a swing-trade pullback and said so here.

name: OverExitOnFailedAddOn
quote: This example also raised the possibility of adding to an existing position. This is a good plan in many cases, but it also makes sense to aggressively adjust the position if that second entry fails by exiting more than was added. In other words, if you were holding 5,000 shares from C and added 2,000 at D, you would exit more than 2,000 on the failure of D.
description: When a pyramided add-on to an existing position fails (the add-on's own stop/failure condition triggers), exit more size than was added at that add-on -- reducing the original core position too, not just closing out the add-on.
pseudocode:
// requires position-history state: size added at the most recent add-on
addOnFailureTriggered && exitSize > mostRecentAddOnSize  // exitSize computed as overExitMultiple * mostRecentAddOnSize
book_order_type: n/a (position-management rule on a stop/failure trigger)

complexity.reason: needs cross-bar position-history state: the size of the most recent add-on and a way to detect that add-on's failure

notes: Grimes gives no exact over-exit ratio, only that it should exceed the added amount; defaulted overExitMultiple to 1.5x the add-on size and said so here.

name: ExitOnExtremeFavorableRangeExpansion
quote: This is the May 2010 Flash Crash. If you are ever holding a position into such an exceptional move, cover part or all of the position into the move. Do not be greedy and do not play for a one-in-a-million event. On those very rare occasions when the market offers windfall profits, take them.
description: If the current bar's move in the position's favor is an extreme outlier relative to normal volatility (range far beyond a multiple of ATR), take the windfall by covering part or all of the position on that bar rather than assuming continuation.
pseudocode:
// long
marketPosition() == 1 && (high[0] - low[0]) >= extremeRangeMultiple * atr(atrLength) && close[0] > ctx.EntryPrice()  // triggers covering part/all of the position
book_order_type: n/a (discretionary windfall exit, mechanized as a range-vs-ATR outlier test)

complexity.reason: a single bar's range compared against a multiple of its ATR, plus a position-direction check

notes: Grimes's example (the May 2010 Flash Crash) is an extreme outlier; extremeRangeMultiple of 4x ATR is a guessed threshold for 'exceptional move,' not a number he gives.

name: MeasuredMoveObjectiveDefinition
quote: A technique used to set an approximate price target for a swing out of consolidation, based on the assumption that future volatility will resemble past volatility. This, and all other ratio-based measures, is better used as a guide than a precise target.
description: Projects a price target for a breakout out of consolidation equal to the breakout level plus the height of the consolidation pattern that preceded it.
pseudocode: patternHeight = highest(high, patternBars) - lowest(low, patternBars); high[0] >= breakoutLevel + patternHeight
book_order_type: limit order at the projected target; mechanized as a bar-extreme test

complexity.reason: needs the height of a preceding consolidation window
